correctness.rationale: Every convex n-gon with n>=4 has a nonacute angle. Centering at the preceding vertex makes distance along the next edge nondecreasing, so those two consecutive edges contribute at most one distinct circle intersection; the other incident edge contributes at most one and each remaining segment at most two, giving 2n-4. For a right/obtuse triangle the same monotonicity gives a center with at most two intersections and small circles give exactly two. For an acute triangle, each boundary point has at least two strict vertex maxima of the distance function, so a level just below the second-largest maximum yields four crossings; a vertex center gives the matching upper bound four.

value.rationale: This gives an explicit complexity-dependent bound for the invariant underlying an open universal-bound problem and settles the complete triangle phase transition. In particular it proves uniform four- and six-intersection bounds for quadrilaterals and pentagons. That is a natural structural cutoff, not an arbitrary finite calculation.
residual_risks: The 2n-4 coefficient is not asserted optimal for larger n.

final_claim: For the Erdős circle-intersection invariant, every convex \(n\)-gon with \(n\ge4\) satisfies \(N(K)\le2n-4\); for triangles, \(N(T)=4\) when acute and \(N(T)=2\) when right or obtuse.
limitations: The linear polygon bound is not claimed sharp for every n.
The universal convex-body bound remains open.
